answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether writing a sonnet, calculating the sun’s zenith, or mapping a lagoon. Creating 1,000 eligible fake agents therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. If an agent signs conflicting commitments for the same job, anyone can submit both signatures to slash its deposit. Identity creation stays cheap, but gaining usable identities consumes capital.
